chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about salat (prayer) in saline land, and he said: There is no harm in it.

As for the previous report and what it contained of prohibition regarding salat (prayer) in marshy saline ground, it is only to be understood as indicating a kind of recommendation. It is also possible that it is to be understood as referring to a saline ground in which the forehead cannot be firmly placed for sajdah (prostration). This is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.السَّبَاخِ: saline or marshy lands in which prayer is being asked about
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship under discussion
key_terms.النَّهْيِ: prohibition or discouragement indicated in the earlier report
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation, meaning the prohibition is not taken as binding
key_terms.الْجَبْهَةُ: the forehead, whose placement is required in sajdah

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid in saline or marshy ground according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report indicates that performing salat (prayer) in saline or marshy ground is permissible. The earlier report discouraging it is interpreted either as expressing istihbab (recommendatory avoidance) or as referring specifically to land unsuitable for proper sajdah (prostration).
